title: Experiment evaluation roadmap and decision funnels for staged rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a repeatable experiment evaluation roadmap and decision funnels (canary -> A/B -> phased rollout) for model and runtime changes. This ticket centralizes milestone definitions, metric thresholds, monitoring playbooks, and stakeholder decision checkpoints so PM/Eng/Design can conduct predictable, low-risk rollouts that map to OKR success metrics. Scope: runtime and model changes that touch production inference (hosted or dedicated). Out of scope: purely internal infra changes with no customer-facing behavior change.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical evaluation matrix exists (metrics, thresholds, weight, direction) and is stored in Confluence with links in this ticket.
Playbook for canary failure detection and automated rollback is implemented and tested in staging with simulated traffic.
Experiment templates (canary, A/B, phased) are added to the Experiment Console and include default dashboards and alerts.
Cross-functional approval flow documented (PM -> Eng -> Reliability -> Legal if needed) and a sign-off checklist is available.
At least one pilot rollout uses the new decision funnels and produces a post-mortem that references this ticket as source-of-truth.

experiment_design_summary: Primary experiment type: staged canary followed by A/B for quality signal validation. Canary: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% over incremental windows with 24-72h observation windows. A/B: 50/50 split for evaluation against quality metrics for up to 7 days. Variants: control (current runtime + model) and treatment (model v2.3 with optimized batching). Data capture: per-request traces, token-level latency, model score tags, and opt-in human eval samples via the evaluation UI.
evaluation_metrics: Latency: p50, p95, p99 (ms) by route and model - primary latency SLOs must not degrade > 20% relative to baseline for canary progression.
Error rate: 5xx + inference failures - must remain < 0.3% absolute increase vs baseline for canary progression.
Quality delta: human-rated relevance score (0-100); treatment must not drop more than 1.5 points absolute vs control in A/B.
Hallucination/safety incidents: reported safety flags per 10k requests - must be <= baseline + 0.1.
Cost/unit: token-cost or GPU util delta - expected improvement or acceptable regression defined per experiment.
rollout_gates: Gate 0 (Pre-canary): design + infra + security sign-off. No deployment without checklist complete.

Gate 1 (Canary->1%): pass automatic canary checks for 24h: p95 latency increase <= 20% AND error delta <= 0.3% AND no new safety incidents. If failed -> immediate rollback to control and a post-rollback investigation.

Gate 2 (1%->5%): extended observation 48h with human-sample review: quality delta <= 1.0 points and no trend of increasing errors. If marginal failure, hold and run remedial tuning; if severe, rollback.
Gate 3 (A/B validation): run 7-day A/B; treatment passes statistical tests for primary quality metric (p<0.05) or meets pre-defined business uplift threshold. If inconclusive, run longer or adjust.
Gate 4 (Phased Ramp to 100%): incremental ramp with automated SLO checks at each step and a mandatory stakeholder sign-off at 25% and 75%.
Rollback Criteria: any gate failure with critical impact (latency p99 > 2x baseline or error rate increase > 1.0% absolute or safety incident spike) -> automatic rollback.
monitoring_playbook: Dashboard: clone 'Experiment Base Template' in Console and attach to experiment with real-time p95/p99, error rate, cost/unit, sample rate of human evaluations.
Automated Alert: p95 latency increase > 30% for 10m -> severity 2; trigger on-call and mute rollout automation.
Automated Alert: error rate increase > 0.5% absolute for 5m -> severity 1; immediate rollback automation kicks in.
Human-in-loop: weekly human eval sampling; review panel includes PM, Eng lead, and Design for subjective quality signals.
Incident Runbook Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/experiments/playbook/runbook (run simulated rolling failures quarterly).
decisions_and_tradeoffs: We choose conservative canary thresholds to prioritize availability over marginal cost savings; this slows ramp times but reduces customer-facing incidents.
A/B statistical significance target set to p<0.05 which may require longer runs for low-traffic routes; trade-off accepted to avoid false positives.
Default human sampling rate set at 0.1% of requests to keep evaluation costs manageable; this may miss rare quality regressions and we will increase sample size for high-risk experiments.
